title: New Orleans Criteria (CT Head)
keywords: persistent anterograde amnesia short-term memory deficit
sources: Haydel MJ, et al. Indications for computed tomography in patients with minor head injury. N Engl J Med. 2000;343(2):100-105
Stiell IG, et al. Comparison of the Canadian CT Head Rule and the New Orleans Criteria in patients with minor head injury. JAMA. 2005;294(12):1511-1518

changelog.change: Initial entry — the 7-item New Orleans Criteria; companion to the Canadian CT Head Rule calculator (per the decision-rules-cspine-ct-head reference build note).

purpose: Identifies which adults with minor head injury (blunt trauma, LOC, and a GCS of 15) need a non-contrast CT head. Highly sensitive (~99-100%) for injury on CT but low specificity — it drives more scans than the Canadian CT Head Rule at similar sensitivity. Any positive item = CT.

items.label: Seizure (witnessed or suspected, after the injury)

interpretation.label: No criteria — CT head not required by the rule in a GCS-15 patient with an otherwise normal exam. Observe and give head-injury discharge advice; the rule was not derived for anticoagulated patients — image them regardless
≥ 1 criterion — obtain a non-contrast CT head

notes: Inclusion: blunt head trauma within 24 h, witnessed loss of consciousness, and GCS 15 at assessment with a normal neurologic exam. Applies only to GCS 15 — a lower GCS gets imaged regardless. Head-to-head (Stiell, JAMA 2005): NOC and the Canadian CT Head Rule are both ~100% sensitive for clinically important injury, but CCHR is markedly more specific (fewer unnecessary CTs) — pick one rule per patient and apply every criterion. Neither rule was derived for patients on anticoagulants/antiplatelets or with a bleeding disorder.
buildNote: Rule — any positive item mandates CT; the count is not a graded risk. Companion to `canadian-ct-head`; both cross-linked from `decision-rules-cspine-ct-head`.
